Subject: [UAI] Wanted: CS and EE majors for graduate studies in Statistics


Wanted: CS and EE majors for graduate studies in Statistics
	University of Washington, Seattle


Please spread the word:

The Statistics Department at the University of Washington welcomes
applications from Computer Science and Electrical Engineering majors
to its graduate program.

****** Why consider a Statistics PhD or MS degree? ******

Statistical thinking is necessary in all disciplines engaged in
drawing information from data. Computer scientists find themselves
increasingly in the position of scientists -- who analyse data
collected by computers -- rather than engineers called to build
systems for entirely artificial environments. Understanding the
sources of uncertainty in the data and correctly dealing with them is
one of the fundamental functions of statistics.

On the other hand, data analysis by computer is now revolutionizing
statistics. So, expertise in computing is an important prerequisite
for creating and applying innovative data analysis tools. New and
exciting areas of research are emerging at the boundary between
statistics, computer science and other sciences like biology and
astronomy. Machine learning, computational biology, data mining,
statistical analysis of social and political phenomena (including the
Internet), environmetrics are a few of them. Demand is rapidly
increasing also for individuals trained to invent, evaluate, and apply
the new tools in these fields.

Collaborative research is essential to Statistics. Most of our faculty
are involved in interdisciplinary research -- follow the links below
for a snapshot of some of the ongoing research projects at UW
Statistics.

Our department recognizes that, along with mathematics, computing is
at the foundation of statistics. It encourages applications from
students with strong mathematical and computing skills. The successful
candidate in our graduate program is one WELL PREPARED TO LEARN
STATISTICS (for instance by a good analythical and computing
background) and able to creatively use it.

Our current graduate students have a variety of backgrounds:
mathematics -- pure and applied, engineering and CS, physics, biology,
management. We appreciate their diversity. Our environment is richer
for their contribution and our graduate program is flexible enough to
allow them to realise each their own potential.


More information --

    * The departmental home page   www.stat.washington.edu 
    * The graduate program pages   http://www.stat.washington.edu/www/graduate/
    * What our graduate students do (at UW and after) 
				   http://www.stat.washington.edu/www/statistician/
    * Our view of the future of statistics 
                                   http://www.stat.washington.edu/www/graduate/view/index.shtml
